title: Quality of Life for Patients With Breast Cancer Brain Metastases and Leptomeningeal Disease
official: Prospective Evaluation of Quality of Life in Patients With Breast Cancer Brain Metastases and Leptomeningeal Disease
summary: Central nervous system (CNS) metastases including breast cancer brain metastases (BCBMs) and leptomeningeal disease (LMD) are common affecting up to 30% of patients with metastatic breast cancer (MBC). The goal of this research is to understand symptom burden and quality of life trajectories in this population and how treatments guide care management decisions.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Be male or female 18 years of age or older.
2. Have stage 4 (metastatic) breast cancer with spread to the brain parenchyma and/or leptomeninges.
3. Have the intention to start or continue anticancer therapy.
4. Be able to provide informed consent.
5. Be able to speak and read English.

Exclusion Criteria:

Participants who are not on any anticancer therapy and are not planning to start any anticancer therapy will be excluded from the study.
